answer_1.quote: We introduce the first end-to-end methods for generating whole SOAP notes based on clinical conversations... Our work builds on a unique corpus... that consists of thousands of transcripts of recorded clinical conversations together with associated SOAP notes...
answer_1.outputs: Full-length SOAP notes (section‑segmented summaries) generated from doctor‑patient conversation transcripts

answer_2.quote: We evaluate the generated SOAP notes using ROUGE scores... Table 3: ROUGE‑1 achieved on test set when using the abstractive models with oracle noteworthy utterances and clusters...

answer_4.quote: We asked trained human annotators to evaluate generated SOAP notes for 45 conversations. Every sentence in each SOAP note was labeled according to various quality dimensions such whether it was factually correct, incoherent, irrelevant, redundant, or placed under an inappropriate section. In addition, we asked two separate questions for rating the overall summary on a scale of 1‑5 for its comprehensiveness and extent of verbatim copying from conversation.
answer_4.guideline: Annotators labeled each sentence for factual correctness, redundancy, irrelevance, incoherence, and correct section placement; they also rated overall comprehensiveness and copying on a 5‑point Likert scale.
